issues.description: Conflicting requirements for the SealSaloon.stock attribute. problem_statement.md (lines 70-73) instructs that SealSaloon should have a final Stock stock initialized in the no-argument constructor (implying an instance-level final field). Later in the same problem statement (lines 77-81) it explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and shared across instances. The solution implements the attribute as a class-level static final field (private static final Stock stock) at src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java:5. This contradiction (instance final vs static final) will confuse students about where and how to declare and initialize the stock field and how the rest of the API (e.g., static vs. instance methods) should interact with it.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction by choosing one clear design and updating the problem statement and UML accordingly. Two viable options: (A) Make stock a shared class resource: update the textual requirement and UML to state 'private static final Stock stock' and instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer; also mark acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice as static (as already done in the solution). OR (B) Make stock an instance final field: remove the static requirements from the problem statement and UML, instruct students to initialize stock in the no-arg constructor, and convert related methods in the examples/tests to instance methods. Update all references in the problem text, UML and example code so they consistently reflect the chosen design.
